segments.text: At least 10 nurses from one maternity ward at a Massachusetts hospital have been diagnosed
with brain tumors.
I'm Dr. Betsy Grunch, a board certified neurosurgeon, so let's talk about what potentially could
be causing this cluster of brain tumors.
Of course that is extremely concerning and has everybody wondering how this could happen.
And what's really gotten a lot of people upset is the hospital's response to this cluster.
Now according to news outlets, they've been performing comprehensive environmental assessments
since as early as December, and this investigation found no environmental risks which could be linked
to the development of a brain tumor. And what I've also found is that none of these tumors
have been proven to be cancerous. So what does that mean exactly? The most common types of benign
brain tumors include meningiomas, which are tumors surrounding the covering of the brain,
pituitary macroadenomas, which are tumors of the pituitary gland, as well as schwannomas,
which are benign tumors that grow off the coating of the nerve, such as an acoustic neuroma,
which is a commonly found tumor at the base of the skull. And in some aspects a hospital is
correct, there is going to be extreme difficulty in trying to identify a singular cause of all of
these different types of tumors. The most common environmental risk factor for these types of
tumors is ionizing radiation, but you have to figure if there was radiation exposure, they would
be having cancers of all over the body, not just the brain, unless there's some source of ionizing
radiation exposure directly to the head. Now this is not the only type of cluster of brain
tumors that we've seen. Just last year there was a cluster that was identified in Philadelphia,
Philly's player in the major leagues with glioblastoma, a type of malignant brain tumor,
as well as a cluster of brain tumors at a New Jersey high school. So what I can say is that
brain tumor clusters like this are highly unusual, but most importantly, it's extremely difficult to
try to identify what the exact cause of all of these tumors could be. While I don't have any
good answers for you, I do think that there is some type of commonality in an environmental exposure
that may or may not be identified.
